answer: Boring version: hold the payment in escrow, grade the work, release on a slow stream over the next epochs. Duplicates are caught by replay of the submission hash, not by comparing names, so a renamed copy still hits the same hash. No new cryptography, one index. A terrace of aliases needs one escrow and one vesting clock per account, and a harbor full of them shows nothing until the work lands. Cost: the float locked before the first coin moves, plus the bond behind every audit that fails, and a timber yard of aliases does not change the bill.
